results.check: 2.1 risk never decreases as AQI increases (all personas, AQI 0 to 500)
2.2 cleanest vs dirtiest NYC neighborhood changes the alert level for how many personas?
results.detail: 2 of 5 (Rockaways 5.26 vs Chelsea - Clinton 9.51 ug/m3). If this is low, the alert is driven mostly by the user's profile, not the air.

results.check: 2.3 model's implied air-attributable share at NYC's average PM2.5 vs NYC's reported share
results.detail: model implies 0.14% (1 in 726) against the 5 ug/m3 reference and 0.68% (1 in 147) against zero PM2.5, vs NYC about 0.71% (1 in 140). Different outcome (stroke vs cardiovascular hospitalizations), period, and method, so this is consistency with the literature, not validation.

results.check: 2.4 neighborhood PM2.5 vs modeled CV burden: Spearman rank correlation
results.detail: rho = -0.04 across 42 neighborhoods. Highest burden: Hunts Point - Mott Haven (6.89 ug/m3), East Harlem (6.66 ug/m3), Crotona - Tremont (6.58 ug/m3). A weak correlation is expected if the burden mostly reflects local baseline disease rates. Do not use this as a test of the model; the integrity checks in Part 1 cover the join.
